concerns.text: The plan proposes generating bootstrap confidence intervals for 'all reported cosine-similarity measurements' (including subspace similarity from FR-002) by 'resampling the token-frequency observation set'. However, the subspace bases are derived via SVD of the unembedding matrix $W_U$ (FR-001), which is independent of the token frequency distribution $f$. Resampling $f$ will not affect the SVD results, rendering the bootstrap CIs for subspace similarity mathematically void (point estimates).

The plan claims that performing correlations on baseline-adjusted shift vectors will 'guarantee independence from raw token frequencies'. This is a contradiction: the shift vector $\Delta h$ is explicitly computed as $W_U^+ 	imes (f_{lang} - f_{uniform})$. It is a direct linear function of the raw token frequencies. While it removes the global mean bias, it is not 'independent' of the frequencies.
